summary: The three imported guarantees are now used to define a total board: gate transcripts plus explicit domain and value output tests force one semantic address, while zero pointers into every rival force uniqueness. The concrete four-column board makes the winner and off-promise distinction intelligible. The local verifier has adaptive query depth logarithmic in m although its variable support is linear. Its reversible evaluator works on arbitrary test-index superpositions. Dominance needs only the actual winner's correctly decoded address; rival labels may be arbitrary. The bounded amplification proof supplies a finite all-input cap and preserves the complete successful original-register state, with ancillary trial histories explicitly separated. All these claims are readable at this encounter; the remaining upper-bound uncertainty is how the weighted tournament finds enough candidates under intransitive comparisons.
